text:
maria: Heads up — ran nightly perf sweep on the CUDA-11/RTX3090 pool and hit a weird kernel flip at seqlen=512 where the runtime picked a fallback SDPA path mid-batch. tail latency +35% for a subset of requests.
kevin: ugh. is this with causal mode on? any reproduction script or small trace?
maria: causal=true. repro is pretty small: set batch=4, seqlen=512, head_dim=30, model=rwkv-ish test. quick command: `RUNTIME_PROFILE=1 ./run_infer --seqlen 512 --batch 4 --heads 48 --head-width 30 --causal` — logs attached.
jonathan: head_width=30 is non-aligned for many kernels, might trigger fallback heuristics. did the kernel picker log which kernel it chose initially vs after flip?
maria: yes — at 00:02:12 it selected flashv2-fast, then at 00:02:12.143 it switched to sdpa-safe. snippet from runtime log: ```[2026-03-15T00:02:12.000Z] kernel_picker: probe flash_candidate (lat 1.9ms)
[2026-03-15T00:02:12.143Z] kernel_picker: fallback to sdpa_safe (lat 3.1ms) cause=unaligned_head_dim
```
kevin: that latency jump matches. did KV cache warmup influence it? any preceding microbatches with different seqlen?
maria: workload is mixed: some requests at 64 then a 512 arrives. we do KV prefix caching; the flip correlates with a request that reused a cached prefix and then appended a long continuation.
jonathan: hmm — two possibilities: (1) probe measurement noise when cache reuse reduces effective memory bandwidth, so probe thinks flash is slower and switches, (2) hysteresis in selector too tight so single noisy sample flips path.
sara: can you dump the probe histograms and the allocator traces? also which SM (compute capability) on that 3090? might be 8.6?
maria: SM 8.6, driver 535.102. here's the probe deltas (p95 in ms): flash_probe: [1.85,1.87,1.82,1.90] sdpa_probe: [2.9,3.05,2.99,3.1] then after cache-reuse flash_probe jumped to 2.95. allocator shows a transient page migration event.
kevin: page migration would reduce the effective streamed throughput — could explain flash kernel suffering more (it relies on contiguous pinned buffers). sdpa path is more resilient to scatter.
johnathan: (typo) jonathan: agreed. solution ideas: add a short minimum-hold period after a successful flash pick (0.5–1s), or make probe compare median over last N samples instead of single-sample decisions. also consider aligning small head widths by padding to 32 on device-side for flash kernels.
maria: can we avoid padding for accuracy-sensitive models? some customers care about exact FLOPs. padding could be opt-in via config flag `prefer_latency_over_exact_layout=true`.
sara: we should instrument how often head-padding would change outputs (should be zero if we only pad internal layout without changing math). Ops team: add opt-in pad transform that is layout-only.
kevin: for immediate mitigation I propose: (A) revert selector to require two consecutive worse samples before switching, (B) emit metric `kernel_switch_due_to_probe_noise` and alert on >3/min, (C) schedule a canary rollout of hold-period=800ms on a small fleet.
maria: testing locally — patched selector to require 2-sample majority, re-ran the repro, flip did not occur. latency stable.
perf-bot: perf-profile summary: baseline (no-change) p50=12.1ms p95=34.2ms; with 2-sample majority p50=12.3ms p95=35.0ms; switching events dropped from 7->0 over 10k requests.
jonathan: nice. follow-up items: INF ticket, add unit for probe comparator, add opt-in head-pad transform, create dashboard panel for probe noise.
maria: created INF-4572 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4572 — includes logs and patch link. assigning to kevin for canary rollout.
kevin: got it, I'll do a 3-node canary with hold-period=800ms and monitor `kernel_switch` metric and tail latency for 6 hours. report back here. :thumbsup:
sara: also add a note to ops-runbook about 3090 page-migration gotchas.
maria: thanks all — will update with canary results.
